Apply for admission to the PhD programme with external funding
Apply for admission to the PhD programme with external funding
If you have secured external funding for a PhD position, you can apply for admission. Your application can be sent as soon as your funding is secured and up until 2 months after starting your PhD project. If you have not yet secured funding or want to apply for a PhD position at UiO, please go back to review the details regarding these steps.
Admission requirements
For admission to the PhD program at the MN Faculty, the following criteria must be met:
§ 5.1.1 Qualifications: Applicants must fulfil the qualifications specified by the Faculty
§ 5.1.3 Grade requirements: Applicants must meet the designated grade requirements.
§ 5.1.4 English language skills: Proficiency in the English language is mandatory.
External funding
Vacant position listings
Externally funded PhD positions can be announced online on the following websites:
Jobbnorge
EURAXESS
Funding schemes
The Research Council of Norway offer funding schemes both for public sector and companies seeking to enhance their research expertise and activity through a PhD candidate project. The project is intended to result in research and development outcomes that strengthen products and/or services for the company/public sector.
You find more information on The Research Council of Norway web pages:
Public sector PhD Scheme
Industrial PhD Scheme
What must the funding cover?
External PhD candidates are required to secure funding for:
Salary equivalent to the standard PhD candidate salary covering three years of full-time study
Research expenses, if necessary for the project.
Financial compensation to UiO. This includes both the follow-up contribution and any potential expenses for the use of research infrastructure at the department.
Follow-up contribution
This financial compensation to UiO covers the University's costs related to the PhD candidate's education. The cost will be invoiced over three years, with one-third due at the start. The above contributions are exempt from Value Added Tax.
Use of research infrastructure
In case the PhD candidate will use research infrastructure at the department (such as laboratory facilities or specialized data computation infrastructure) the external party cover potential expenses. Costs are based on the TDI model and the Leased Space model.
Funds from foreign foundations or universities
If you have funds from foreign foundations or universities, you must have a minimum of NOK 25 000 per month to cover both accommodation and living expenses during your stay in Norway.
Apply for admission
Once you have secured external funding, you can apply for admission. You are required to submit your admission application through an online form no later than 2 months after starting your PhD project.
The complete application consists of a project description, a completed admission form, your CV and other relevant supporting documents. You and your supervisors collaborate on your admission application and project description.
The online submission form also serves as a checklist and will require you to provide all required documents.
Submit your application
Prepare your research proposal
The project description is the key part of your application and must demonstrate good academic quality. The project description (from 4 to 10 pages) must adhere to the respective department’s/unit’s project description guidelines.

Compile all the required supporting documents
You will be asked to upload the following attachments:
The complete admission form (.pdf)
The project description
Your CV
In addition, for externally employed candidates:
Agreement of cooperation with the external institution (Contact your affiliated department/unit for the agreement form and information)
In addition, for PhD candidates funded by international stipends:
Documentation of a granted stipend that secure funding for the whole PhD period
In addition, if relevant:
A list of your publications
Course description of special syllabus/-i and/or research course/-s you are including in your educational component
Confirmation of already passed courses you are including in your educational component
English language skills test, for international applicants (some are exempt from the requirements. For more information, see § 5.1.4 English language skills)
REK approval and/or recommendation from Sikt (Norwegian Agency for Shared Services in Education and Research) for projects that will include processing of personal data or conduct health-related research
PhD candidates planning to spend less than 1 year at UiO must attach an application for reduced residence duty authored by the UiO associated principal or co-supervisor arguing how the external institution provides a rigorous research environment and that the academic demands for supervision are sustained. Consult the Faculty regulations § 5.1.6.5 Residency for details
In addition, for applicants with bachelor’s and master’s degrees outside the University of Oslo:
Copies of diplomas for bachelor’s and master’s degrees, supplemented with transcripts showing which courses are included in both degrees
Official description of the grading structure from the degree conferring institution (for applicants with international education)
In addition, for candidates who apply for having an external principal supervisor (not employed at UiO or UNIS):
The external principal supervisor's CV and publication list
An application to have an external principal supervisor (.docx)
Submission of original documents
You may be requested to provide original documents for your bachelor's and master's degrees, along with accompanying transcripts.
Special requirements
If you have a completed degree from one of the following countries, you must provide original documents for your degree, along with accompanying transcript prior to applying for admission.
Cameroon, Canada, China, Ethiopia, Ghana, Nigeria, Tanzania, The Republic of the Philippines, USA.
The qualification documents must be sent directly from the educational institution to the MN Faculty administration at the following address:
The Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences, PhD office
PO Box 1032 Blindern
NO-0315 Oslo
Norway
Applicants with completed degrees from China can, instead of sending original diplomas, provide a CDGDC or CHESICC verification.
Applicants with completed degrees from Republic of the Philippines and USA can ask the educational institution to send original diplomas digitally to phd-godkjenning@mn.uio.no, if they offer this service.
Review our learning outcomes
During the application process, it is important to consult the PhD programme learning outcomes. Ensure that your project and courses align with and contribute to achieving the expected learning outcomes as outlined in the PhD programme description.
See more information about the learning outcomes
Minimum progress and working hours
A minimum of 50% of your working hours should be dedicated to working with your PhD. It is therefore not possible to plan completion of the PhD programme over a period of more than 6 years.
Affiliation, residency and supervision
All external PhD candidates are required to establish affiliation with a research community within our Faculty. This entails both supervision from UiO and residence duty.
Supervision
All externally funded PhD candidates must have at least one supervisor from the MN faculty. You can reach out to a potential supervisor at the MN faculty either before or after securing your funding.
Usually the supervisor from the MN faculty is the principal supervisor. For detailed information, please refer to the Faculty regulations § 7.3 on The principal supervisor.
See more information about PhD supervision
The induction conversation
At the initial stage of the supervision, you and your main supervisor must agree on the framework for the supervision, i.e. progress plan and expectations for guidance etc. Having conducted the mandatory induction conversation is a requirement for admission.
See more information about the induction conversation
Residency requirements
External candidates are expected to spend a total of 12 months at UiO to facilitate close interaction with their UiO supervisor(s) and the local research environment. During this period, the department will provide office space and infrastructure on the same terms as for internal doctoral candidates. For detailed information, please refer to the Faculty regulations § 5.1.6.5 on Residency.
Decide which courses you want to take
In the application form, you must provide a list of the courses you want to take as part of your PhD.
See more information about the courses and the educational component of your PhD
What happens after I have submitted the application?
Once you have submitted your admission application, you will receive a confirmation email from us. There is no further action required on your part unless your department/unit contacts you for additional information or changes.
Your admission application will undergo evaluation by the PhD council at your department before being forwarded to the Faculty for final approval. The purpose of the evaluation is to check that all formal requirements have been met, ensure the quality of your project, and enable adjustments at an early stage.
Official letter of admission
Following approval at the Faculty, you will receive an official letter of admission. This confirmation letter serves as your formal agreement with the Faculty.
Changes to the PhD agreement
You can make changes to your PhD agreement after the admission application has been approved, but you must apply to have the changes approved.
See more information about making changes to the PhD agreement
